title: LegiVellum principal and authority model v1
description: The identities the protocol distinguishes, where each one lives, and which transitions each role may propose. ReceiptGate loads this and evaluates it; it is not a description of what ReceiptGate does. Receipts keep their four principal fields unchanged -- the richer model lives in the obligation and custody projections, and every projection field is reconstructible from the immutable ledger so the projection is never a second source of truth.

identities.question: Who is the outcome owed to?
Who may observe this obligation and its evidence?
identities.derived_from: authenticated tenant/authority at commit time, recorded as receipt.tenant_id
identities.note: Must derive from authenticated identity, never from a caller-supplied string. This is the identity the schema had no field for; it is reconstructible because tenant_id is server-assigned and present on every receipt.

identities.question: Who currently holds responsibility?
identities.derived_from: receipt.recipient_ai on the ACCEPT receipt, then receipt.escalation_to on each committed transfer
identities.note: Distinct from recipient_ai as an inbox routing key. Conflating them is why a completion could close an obligation its issuer never held.

identities.question: Who performed this transition?
identities.note: Bound server-side. A component holding a shared key must not be able to assert that some other principal performed a transition.

identities.question: Which service emitted the protocol operation?
identities.derived_from: receipt.source_system, bound to the authenticated service identity

principal.description: An external actor that may authorize work.

delegate.description: A planning authority. May mint obligations.

worker.description: Executes leased work. May take and discharge custody but may not authorize new obligations for others.

service.description: An infrastructure component acting on its own behalf.

observer.description: Read-only. May observe within its visibility scope and may propose nothing.

rules.statement: COMPLETE and ESCALATE may be proposed only by the current custodian of the obligation.
RECOVER reclaims an obligation whose custodian is absent; it is proposed by another party and is only legal from OVERDUE.
An observer role may never propose a governance transition, regardless of credential.
A principal may observe an obligation only when its authenticated visibility scope matches the obligation's visibility_principal.
transition_actor, service_emitter and visibility_principal are bound from authenticated context and any conflicting caller-supplied value is rejected rather than honoured.
